name: Performance Profiling Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in performance profiling work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.
content:
This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in performance profiling work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Re-check edge cases relevant to performance profiling (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
2. Keep performance profiling outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
3. Check that performance profiling terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
4. Keep performance profiling changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
5. Prefer the simplest performance profiling approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
6. Document any non-obvious performance profiling decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
7. Measure before optimizing any performance profiling bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
8. Surface known limitations of a chosen performance profiling approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
9. Prefer explicit, readable performance profiling solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
10. When performance profiling decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
11. When multiple performance profiling strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
12. When performance profiling guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not silently drop performance profiling edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not apply generic performance profiling advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not skip documenting performance profiling assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Avoid introducing new performance profiling abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Avoid mixing unrelated performance profiling concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for performance profiling, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
